about: Employees workload for tools/sample_db_bench.py. origin 'upstream-view': the views of upstream employees.sql and objects.sql (name = upstream view name), adapted to BigQuery SQL as 'adaptation' says; 'upstream-procedure': the SELECTs of the upstream stored functions and of the show_departments procedure with their parameters bound to the values in 'adaptation'; 'upstream-test': the record-count comparison of upstream's test_employees_md5.sql, adapted (its checksum probes use MySQL session variables and are checked by the harness instead, not run through the rewrites); 'authored': written for this eval. The adapted upstream queries are adaptations of CC BY-SA 3.0 text and are shared under the same licence (see NOTICE.md).

queries.name: dept_emp_latest_date
queries.adaptation: none beyond the MySQL statement's CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW header
queries.sql:
SELECT emp_no, MAX(from_date) AS from_date, MAX(to_date) AS to_date
FROM dept_emp
GROUP BY emp_no
features: aggregation on part of a key

queries.name: current_dept_emp
queries.adaptation: the view dept_emp_latest_date it reads is inlined as a derived table (the harness keeps the loaded database read-only, so no view is created); the MySQL # comment is dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT l.emp_no, d.dept_no, l.from_date, l.to_date
FROM dept_emp AS d
INNER JOIN (SELECT emp_no, MAX(from_date) AS from_date, MAX(to_date) AS to_date FROM dept_emp GROUP BY emp_no) AS l
  ON d.emp_no = l.emp_no AND d.from_date = l.from_date AND l.to_date = d.to_date

queries.name: v_full_employees
queries.adaptation: the stored function emp_dept_name(emp_no) (which calls emp_dept_id) is inlined as the correlated scalar subqueries of the two function bodies, MySQL's `set @max_date` bookkeeping dropped
queries.sql:
SELECT e.emp_no, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.birth_date, e.gender, e.hire_date,
  (SELECT dep.dept_name FROM departments AS dep WHERE dep.dept_no = (SELECT de.dept_no FROM dept_emp AS de WHERE de.emp_no = e.emp_no AND de.from_date = (SELECT MAX(de2.from_date) FROM dept_emp AS de2 WHERE de2.emp_no = e.emp_no) LIMIT 1)) AS department
FROM employees AS e

queries.name: v_full_departments
queries.adaptation: the stored function current_manager(dept_no) (which calls emp_name) is inlined as the correlated scalar subqueries of the two function bodies
queries.sql:
SELECT d.dept_no, d.dept_name, (SELECT CONCAT(e.first_name, ' ', e.last_name) FROM employees AS e WHERE e.emp_no = (SELECT m.emp_no FROM dept_manager AS m WHERE m.dept_no = d.dept_no AND m.from_date = (SELECT MAX(m2.from_date) FROM dept_manager AS m2 WHERE m2.dept_no = d.dept_no) LIMIT 1)) AS manager
FROM departments AS d

queries.adaptation: emp_name is inlined; parameter dept_id bound to 'd005'
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT CONCAT(e.first_name, ' ', e.last_name) FROM employees AS e WHERE e.emp_no = (SELECT m.emp_no FROM dept_manager AS m WHERE m.dept_no = 'd005' AND m.from_date = (SELECT MAX(m2.from_date) FROM dept_manager AS m2 WHERE m2.dept_no = 'd005') LIMIT 1)) AS manager

queries.name: show_departments
queries.adaptation: the procedure's temporary tables department_max_date and department_people become CTEs, v_full_departments is inlined; MySQL accepts the non-aggregated dept_name and manager under GROUP BY dept_no, BigQuery needs them in the GROUP BY
queries.sql:
WITH department_max_date AS (
  SELECT emp_no, MAX(from_date) AS dept_from_date, MAX(to_date) AS dept_to_date FROM dept_emp GROUP BY emp_no
),
department_people AS (
  SELECT dmd.emp_no, de.dept_no
  FROM department_max_date AS dmd
  INNER JOIN dept_emp AS de ON dmd.dept_from_date = de.from_date AND dmd.dept_to_date = de.to_date AND dmd.emp_no = de.emp_no
),
v_full_departments AS (
  SELECT d.dept_no, d.dept_name, (SELECT CONCAT(e.first_name, ' ', e.last_name) FROM employees AS e WHERE e.emp_no = (SELECT m.emp_no FROM dept_manager AS m WHERE m.dept_no = d.dept_no AND m.from_date = (SELECT MAX(m2.from_date) FROM dept_manager AS m2 WHERE m2.dept_no = d.dept_no) LIMIT 1)) AS manager FROM departments AS d
)
SELECT v.dept_no, v.dept_name, v.manager, COUNT(*) AS employees
FROM v_full_departments AS v
INNER JOIN department_people AS p ON v.dept_no = p.dept_no
GROUP BY v.dept_no, v.dept_name, v.manager

queries.name: test_employees_md5.sql
queries.adaptation: the test script's comparison of expected_values with found_values (SELECT e.table_name, IF(e.recs = f.recs, 'OK', 'not ok')), with both tables as inline UNION ALL selects (expected counts from the script's INSERT INTO expected_values, found counts from its COUNT(*) subqueries) and IF written as CASE
queries.sql:
SELECT e.table_name, CASE WHEN e.recs = f.recs THEN 'OK' ELSE 'not ok' END AS records_match
FROM (
  SELECT 'employees' AS table_name, 300024 AS recs UNION ALL SELECT 'departments', 9 UNION ALL SELECT 'dept_manager', 24
  UNION ALL SELECT 'dept_emp', 331603 UNION ALL SELECT 'titles', 443308 UNION ALL SELECT 'salaries', 2844047
) AS e
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT 'employees' AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS recs FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT 'departments', COUNT(*) FROM departments
  UNION ALL SELECT 'dept_manager', COUNT(*) FROM dept_manager UNION ALL SELECT 'dept_emp', COUNT(*) FROM dept_emp
  UNION ALL SELECT 'titles', COUNT(*) FROM titles UNION ALL SELECT 'salaries', COUNT(*) FROM salaries
) AS f ON e.table_name = f.table_name
ORDER BY e.table_name
SELECT DISTINCT emp_no, first_name, last_name FROM employees
